evals.prompt: Define indexing strategy as this skill teaches it. Include the idea of a maintained access path, the index portfolio, and the read benefit versus write/storage/maintenance cost.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not define indexing as adding an index for every filtered column.

evals.prompt: Explain how B-tree, hash, GIN, GiST, SP-GiST, BRIN, Bloom, columnstore, LSM-family, and vector indexes differ by the access pattern they make cheap.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not say B-tree is always the right structure or that vector indexes are exact.

evals.prompt: Why is the goal a small explainable index portfolio rather than many per-column indexes? Name at least five costs every extra index can impose.

A team has one slow SQL statement and asks whether to add an index, then separately asks how to create the chosen index online in production. Which part belongs to query-optimization, which part belongs to indexing-strategy, which part belongs to database-migration, and why?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not let indexing-strategy own slow-query diagnosis or live migration lock/rollback mechanics.

evals.prompt: Classify these concerns as indexing-strategy, query-optimization, database-migration, data-modeling, or sharding-strategy: column order for a composite index, EXPLAIN ANALYZE for one bad query, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY rollout, deciding tenant_id as a shard key, generated column versus expression index, and entity key design.
Use the back-of-the-book index analogy to explain why indexes speed some lookups but become harmful when the book has too many maintained indexes.

A workload filters by tenant_id equality, sorts by created_at descending, and ranges over status; a teammate wants the most selective column first. Apply the skill to choose a composite-index order and explain the trap.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not repeat the most-selective-first myth as the governing rule.

evals.prompt: Correct this statement: 'The database has an index, so the planner will use it, and if it does not then we should add another one.'
evals.negative_expectation: Must not skip plan evidence, selectivity, expression/type mismatch, stale statistics, or unused-index cost.
